strategy.summary: Reproduce the buffered-iterator bug in numpy.unravel_index for (N,1) intp input by building the buggy commit c40c6dc1c863 from source and running the two developer tests added by the fix. The nditer test exercises remove_multi_index on a buffered iterator over an (N,1) array, and the index_tricks test checks the unravel/ravel round trip beyond the buffer boundary. Both should fail on the buggy build and pass on the fixed build.

pinned_because: pytest and hypothesis are documented in README.md with no version constraint and no era-inferred ceiling, so the latest releases compatible with the checked-out tree are chosen rather than pinned
Python version was not stated by the evidence, so the interpreter is whatever the build-capable numpy tree supports on this machine
numpy is built from source because the fix lives in C (nditer_constr.c), so an installed wheel cannot reproduce the buggy or fixed behaviour

strategy.test_command: python -m pytest numpy/_core/tests/test_nditer.py -k remove_multi_index_buffered -q && python -m pytest numpy/lib/tests/test_index_tricks.py -k buffer_boundary -q
strategy.reproducing_test: numpy/_core/tests/test_nditer.py::test_iter_remove_multi_index_buffered (arange(10).reshape(10,1), nditer with buffered and multi_index, buffersize=5, remove_multi_index, enable_external_loop, then concatenate chunks and compare to a.ravel()); plus numpy/lib/tests/test_index_tricks.py test_unravel_index_buffer_boundary (np.arange(10_000, dtype=np.intp)[:, None] unravelled with shape (100,100) and round-tripped through ravel_multi_index)
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision c40c6dc1c863 both tests FAIL: the nditer test's concatenated chunks differ from a.ravel() because the buffered iterator mishandles the size-one inner axis with zero stride after remove_multi_index, and the index_tricks round trip does not recover the indices beyond the buffer boundary. On the fixed revision (the PR's nditer_constr.c change) both tests PASS.
strategy.numerical_probe: np.arange(8194, dtype=np.intp)[:, None].copy() unravelled with shape (1000,1000), then ravel_multi_index round trip, checking position 8193 for the expected value 8193

input_output_examples.input: indices_2d = np.arange(8194, dtype=np.intp)[:, None].copy(); np.unravel_index(indices_2d, (1000, 1000)) evaluated at position 8193
indices_2d = np.arange(8194, dtype=np.intp)[:, None].copy(); np.ravel_multi_index(np.unravel_index(indices_2d, (1000, 1000)), (1000, 1000)) evaluated at position 8193

risks: The bug requires 64-bit intp and a buffered iterator path; on 32-bit platforms or builds where the buffer size differs, the behaviour may not appear and the test may pass on the buggy revision too.

The index_tricks test sits in a class whose name was not given in the diff context; the -k selector avoids depending on the class name, but the test file must still be collected from numpy/lib/tests/test_index_tricks.py.

The reproducing behaviour was observed with the numpy-level reproducer; no sanitiser or special threading was stated, so none is planned, but a build with a different compiler or optimisation level could mask the stride-coalescing defect.
The evidence's test_commands entry (python -c numpy.test()) is not a pytest selector and was not used; the test runs above rely on pytest selection by name.
Building numpy from source needs a C compiler, meson and ninja available; none were specified in the evidence, so build failure is possible if the toolchain is missing.
Dependency versions for pytest and hypothesis are unbounded in the evidence; a much newer pytest could change collection behaviour, though unlikely to affect the numerical transition.

oracle.reference_source: round-trip property: ravel_multi_index(unravel_index(i, shape), shape) must equal i, and the 1-D control input gives the reference coordinates
oracle.why: unravel_index and ravel_multi_index operate on integer intp indices, so exact equality is the correct comparison and no tolerance applies

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On c40c6dc1c863 the nditer test's concatenated chunks disagree with a.ravel() at the affected positions, so assert_array_equal raises AssertionError; the index_tricks test's assert_array_equal on the round-tripped indices raises AssertionError because the value at the boundary is one less than the index (8192 instead of 8193 in the reproducer pattern).
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision both assertions hold: the buffered iterator yields the full ravelled sequence and the unravel/ravel round trip returns the original indices across the buffer boundary.
